analysis.title: Weekly Economic Roundup, 2 November 2026
key_insights: PNC says the AI-related capex cycle is shaping up to be one of the largest on record and is giving a significant boost to domestic demand, even though a large share of AI capex is imported chips and equipment that do not directly add to real GDP growth.

Business capex has begun to broaden beyond AI over the past few quarters. Industrial and transportation equipment investment has improved markedly, and structures investment outside data centers has strengthened modestly from a weak base.

Other evidence of broadening: manufacturers' capex intentions for next year have turned higher, commercial lending and credit demand have improved, and core factory orders excluding aircraft and AI-related components have accelerated.

PNC names two drivers of the non-AI capex pickup. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act restored permanent 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying capex, which raises after-tax returns and has likely pulled some spending into 2026. Tariff uncertainty, which chilled investment in 2025, is lessening.
AI remains the dominant driver of capex in 2026, but PNC sees the non-AI improvement pointing to a broader base of growth heading into 2027.
PNC names continued fed funds rate hikes and an equity market correction as the largest risks to the capex outlook.
AI-related spending has helped offset outright declines in non-AI business capex in prior years. Stock market strength has also supported consumer spending through wealth effects.

The week's data calendar includes ISM Manufacturing (Mon 11/2), JOLTS and Factory Orders (Tue 11/3), ADP, trade balance, ISM Services and the Treasury quarterly refunding (Wed 11/4), productivity, unit labor costs and jobless claims (Thu 11/5), and October payrolls, unemployment and Michigan sentiment (Fri 11/6).

sector_views.rationale: Industrial and transportation equipment investment has improved markedly, and manufacturers' capex intentions for next year have turned higher.

macro_indicators.interpretation: PNC expects a slightly faster expansion in manufacturing amid the continued AI buildout and data center construction. Consensus is 54.5, last actual 55.5.
PNC projects gains to accelerate from 29k to a level slightly above the three-month moving average.
PNC projects the rate unchanged with layoffs remaining low.
Private payrolls are forecast to expand at a slightly slower pace than the prior 90k on a moderation in weekly ADP gains.
PNC expects services activity to moderate slightly in line with slower services spending growth. The calendar table rounds PNC's figure to 55.
Claims are forecast to stay just below 200,000 and in line with the four-week average.
Output is estimated up 3.8% with hours up 1.3%, giving productivity growth of 2.5% versus 1.4% last period.
Hourly compensation growth is estimated at 3.7%, leaving unit labor costs on par with Q2 growth.
A wider goods deficit more than offsets a slightly improved services surplus, widening the gap by a little over 2.5% m/m from -$105.6b.
Orders are projected to have surged mainly on a sharp rise in aircraft orders in the advance durable goods report.
Spending is forecast to give back some of August's strength, with residential building the primary drag.
Auto sales are expected to pick up slightly on increased dealer incentives.
Sentiment is projected to drop slightly on uncertainty from tariffs, the Middle East conflict and the mid-term elections. The calendar table lists PNC at 48.
Credit is expected to expand faster than the prior $8.281b on robust consumer spending.

macro_indicators.indicator: Nonfarm business capex growth contribution, AI-related vs non-AI (change between 2025Q1-26Q1 and 2026Q2-26Q3)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The non-AI contribution to capex growth rose by about three times as much as the AI contribution versus the earlier period, per Figure 2.
Nonresidential fixed investment growth accelerated between the two periods.

risk_factors: Continued fed funds rate hikes are one of the largest risks to the capex outlook.
An equity market correction is one of the largest risks to the capex outlook.
A large share of AI capex is imported equipment, so it adds less to real GDP growth than its size implies.
Consumer sentiment faces uncertainty from tariffs, the Middle East conflict and the mid-term elections.
charts_described: Figure 2 shows nonresidential fixed investment growth rising from +6.8% in 2025Q1-26Q1 to +10.9% in 2026Q2-26Q3, with the AI-related contribution up +1.0pp and the non-AI contribution up +3.0pp.
geopolitical: Tariff uncertainty, which weighed on 2025 investment, is lessening.
PNC cites uncertainty from tariffs, the Middle East conflict and the mid-term elections as a drag on November consumer sentiment.

tension_points.bull_case: Non-AI capex is improving. Industrial and transportation equipment investment is up, manufacturers' capex intentions are higher, C&I lending and credit demand have improved, and OBBBA bonus depreciation plus fading tariff uncertainty support a broader base of growth into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Continued fed funds rate hikes or an equity market correction are the largest risks to the capex outlook. Construction outside data centers remains weak, and much of AI capex is imported and adds little to real GDP.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued fed funds rate hikes or a correction in equity markets.
